effect: Anti-apoptotic, pro-angiogenic, pro-survival — the single most consistently reported MSC-EV miRNA across regenerative contexts.
caveat: Among the most abundant miRNAs in MSC-EV cargo generally, not a marker specific to regenerative signaling — an 'enrichment' claim needs a naive-EV or non-MSC-EV control to mean anything.
keyCitation: Zhu et al., 2017, J Cell Mol Med (MSC-EV miR-21, PTEN/PI3K-Akt cardioprotection)

effect: Pro-angiogenic, supports endothelial barrier integrity.
caveat: Foundational mechanistic work (Fish et al.) is endothelial-cell biology, not MSC-EV-specific — the MSC-EV cargo literature builds on it rather than originating it.
keyCitation: Fish et al., 2008, Dev Cell (foundational, non-MSC); Tao et al., 2017, Theranostics (BMSC-exosome miR-126-3p, diabetic wound)

effect: Pro-angiogenic; also reported for neurite outgrowth in CNS contexts.
caveat: RASA1 is a RasGAP acting on Ras/MAPK signaling, not strictly the PI3K-Akt axis — grouped here with the closest recurring node, not a clean fit.
keyCitation: Katare et al., 2014, Circ Res (stem-cell-derived exosomal miR-132, cardiac angiogenesis)

effect: Canonically anti-inflammatory via NF-κB dampening, but direction of net effect on inflammation and downstream tissue outcome varies by model and dose.
caveat: Reversal is dose- and context-dependent — the same miR-146a delivery has been reported anti-inflammatory in some macrophage/inflammation models and associated with different, sometimes opposing, downstream effects in others. Do not treat 'anti-inflammatory' as a fixed label for this miRNA without checking the specific model.
keyCitation: Multiple independent reports of direction-of-effect divergence; representative primary sources need direct verification before citing a specific reversal claim externally.

effect: Regulates apoptosis and proliferation via p53 pathway components; reported both pro-survival (protective, anti-apoptotic) and growth-suppressive depending on target-cell context.
caveat: One of the clearer documented direction-of-effect reversals in this cargo set — p53-axis regulation by miR-125b is well known in the oncology literature to flip between tumor-suppressive and oncogenic roles depending on cell type, and MSC-EV regenerative contexts inherit that same ambiguity rather than resolving it.
keyCitation: p53/BAK1 targeting is well established generally; the specific MSC-EV regenerative-context reversal citations need direct verification before external use.

effect: Anti-fibrotic — suppresses collagen deposition and extracellular-matrix accumulation; the clearest TGF-β/SMAD-axis counterweight in this cargo set.
caveat: Foundational target validation (van Rooij et al.) is direct cardiac-tissue miRNA biology, not MSC-EV cargo transfer specifically — treat as the mechanistic basis the MSC-EV literature draws on.
keyCitation: van Rooij et al., 2008, PNAS (miR-29 and cardiac fibrosis via collagen targeting — foundational, non-MSC)

effect: Differentiation-promoting, anti-proliferative tumor-suppressor family; regulates the stemness-to-senescence transition broadly across tissues.
caveat: Family-level entry covering multiple mature let-7 isoforms with overlapping but not identical targets. The documented direction-of-effect reversal is specific to the let-7b isoform (pro- vs. anti-angiogenic reported in different studies) — do not assume it generalizes to the whole family.
keyCitation: Roush & Slack, 2008, Trends Cell Biol (let-7 family review, foundational, non-MSC); let-7b-specific reversal citations need direct verification.

effect: The archetypal 'hypoxamir' — induced under hypoxic preconditioning, pro-angiogenic and pro-survival under ischemic conditions.
caveat: Effect and abundance are strongly dependent on whether the parental MSCs were hypoxia-preconditioned before EV harvest — normoxic-culture MSC-EVs carry substantially less miR-210, and results don't transfer across culture conditions.
keyCitation: Chan & Loscalzo, 2010, Cell Cycle (miR-210 as 'hypoxamir', foundational review, non-MSC-specific)

effect: Promotes proliferation and reduces apoptosis via p27/p57 suppression; also reported to modulate angiogenesis.
caveat: Foundational target-validation work is oncology-derived (proliferation control), not MSC-EV-specific — the regenerative-context application is a later extension.
keyCitation: le Sage et al., 2007, EMBO J (miR-221/222 regulation of p27Kip1 — foundational, non-MSC)

effect: Promotes neurite outgrowth and neural plasticity; anti-fibrotic via CTGF suppression.
caveat: The strongest single MSC-EV in-vivo functional-transfer demonstration in this cargo set (rat stroke model, direct EV-mediated transfer shown), which is why it's a common reference point in the stoichiometry debate about whether EV miRNA cargo can be functionally meaningful at reported copy numbers.
keyCitation: Xin et al., 2013, Stem Cells (MSC-exosome miR-133b transfer, neural plasticity and functional recovery after stroke in rats)

effect: Cluster-level pro-angiogenic and pro-neurogenic effect via suppression of anti-angiogenic targets (CTGF, TSP1) alongside direct PTEN suppression.
caveat: Cluster of six co-transcribed miRNAs (17, 18a, 19a, 19b, 20a, 92a) reported as a unit in most MSC-EV work — individual-member contributions are not always separated. The documented direction-of-effect reversal in this cargo set is specific to the miR-92a member, not the cluster as a whole.
keyCitation: Xin et al., 2017, Stem Cells (MSC-exosome miR-17-92 cluster enrichment, neuroplasticity and functional recovery after stroke in rats)

effect: Muscle-enriched miRNA; promotes myoblast survival/regeneration and is separately reported cardioprotective via the same PTEN axis.
caveat: Foundational work establishes this as a muscle-tissue-intrinsic miRNA (myomiR), not an MSC-EV discovery — MSC-EV cargo studies build on that baseline biology.
keyCitation: Small et al., 2010, PNAS (miR-486 regulation of PI3K/Akt signaling via PTEN, muscle-enriched — foundational, non-MSC)

effect: Anti-apoptotic and anti-fibrotic in cardiac contexts, reported to act partly through HMGB1-mediated inflammatory signaling suppression.
caveat: Lower citation confidence than most entries in this file — the foundational cardiac-hypertrophy role of miR-22 is well established, but the specific MSC-EV cargo delivery mechanism is a thinner literature and needs direct verification before use.
keyCitation: Huang et al., 2013, Circ Res (miR-22 and cardiac hypertrophy — foundational, non-MSC-EV-specific; MSC-EV-specific citation not confidently recalled)

effect: Induces autophagy via mTOR suppression; reported neuroprotective and (separately, in tumor angiogenesis literature) anti-angiogenic depending on context.
caveat: The anti-angiogenic mTOR-suppression literature for this miRNA is largely tumor-biology work, not regenerative-medicine work — the neuroprotective/autophagy framing used here is the regenerative-context reading, and the two literatures shouldn't be conflated.
keyCitation: Grundmann et al., 2011, Circulation (miR-100 regulation of neovascularization via mTOR suppression — foundational, non-MSC-EV-specific)

effect: Family-level entry (181a/b/c/d) — reported roles in myogenesis, immune modulation, and (miR-181c specifically) mitochondrial gene regulation.
caveat: Family members have distinct, sometimes non-overlapping target sets — treating 'miR-181' as one biological entity for scoring purposes understates real isoform-level heterogeneity. Isoform should be specified before any claim is used downstream of this record.
keyCitation: Indrieri et al., 2020, EMBO Mol Med (miR-181a/b and mitochondrial disease models — moderate citation confidence, verify directly)

effect: Anti-apoptotic cardioprotection via Bim suppression.
caveat: Engineered/loaded cargo — enriched via parental-cell genetic modification (GATA-4 overexpression), not representative of naive MSC-EV content. Per the literature agent's standing rule, findings here do not transfer to an unloaded/naive product without separate confirmation.
keyCitation: Yu et al., 2015, Int J Cardiol (GATA-4-overexpressing MSC exosomes as a reservoir of anti-apoptotic miRNAs, cardioprotection)

effect: Anti-apoptotic and anti-inflammatory (macrophage polarization) cardioprotection; co-reported alongside miR-24 in the same engineered-cargo model.
caveat: Engineered/loaded cargo — same GATA-4-overexpression construct as miR-24 above. Also a native member of the miR-17-92 cluster (see that entry) — the engineered version here is deliberately enriched beyond native cluster levels, so this is not simply 'more of the same cargo.'
keyCitation: Yu et al., 2015, Int J Cardiol (GATA-4-overexpressing MSC exosomes, miR-19a, PTEN/SOCS1, cardioprotection)

effect: Chondroprotective, anti-catabolic in osteoarthritis models — reported to suppress Wnt-pathway-driven cartilage degradation.
caveat: Engineered/loaded cargo, and this is the lowest-confidence citation in the file — the target/pathway assignment is directionally consistent with the broader engineered-MSC-EV cartilage literature but the specific primary paper was not confidently recalled. Verify before relying on this entry for anything beyond a placeholder.
keyCitation: Not confidently recalled — requires a direct literature search before citing; tentatively associated with engineered MSC-EV osteoarthritis chondroprotection studies.

effect: Native miR-214-3p (notably from osteoclast-derived EVs) suppresses osteoblastic bone formation via ATF4; the engineered regenerative application uses an anti-miR-214-3p construct loaded into MSC-EVs to counteract that suppression and promote osteogenesis.
caveat: Direction of effect depends entirely on whether the cargo is native miR-214-3p (bone-formation-suppressive, originally characterized in osteoclast-derived EVs, not MSC-EVs) or an engineered anti-miR-214-3p construct (bone-formation-promoting). These are opposite interventions sharing one entry — do not read 'effect' without checking which construct a given source used.
keyCitation: Sun et al., 2016, J Extracell Vesicles / Bone Research (osteoclast-derived exosomal miR-214-3p inhibits osteoblastic bone formation via ATF4 — the suppressive/native finding this engineered application is designed to counteract)

effect: Maintains pluripotency and promotes reprogramming efficiency by driving a rapid G1/S cell-cycle transition characteristic of pluripotent cells.
caveat: The foundational literature is about the miRNA itself (transfection/expression), not EV-mediated transfer — whether ESC/iPSC-EVs carry functionally sufficient miR-302 cargo to reproduce these effects is a separate, less-established question from the direct-expression literature this citation reflects.
keyCitation: Judson et al., 2009, Nat Biotechnol (embryonic-stem-cell-specific microRNAs, including the miR-302 cluster, promote induced pluripotency)

effect: Human-ESC-specific cluster supporting proliferation and pluripotency maintenance via p21 and Hippo-pathway (LATS2) suppression.
caveat: This cluster's largest, best-established literature is oncology (germ-cell-tumor biomarker), not regenerative medicine — the regenerative framing here is a minority use case within the broader miR-371-373 literature and should not be assumed to carry the same weight of evidence.
keyCitation: Voorhoeve et al., 2006, Cell (miR-372/373 as oncogenes in testicular germ-cell tumors — the field's dominant citation for this cluster, not a regenerative-medicine paper)

effect: Drives G1/S transition and self-renewal in mouse ESCs; regulates de novo DNA methylation indirectly via RBL2 suppression of DNMT3A/B.
caveat: Mouse-specific cluster with no direct human ortholog — miR-371-373 is the human-ESC functional analogue, not the same sequence. Do not treat findings here as transferable to human cells without that substitution already made in the source study.
keyCitation: Sinkkonen et al., 2008, Nat Struct Mol Biol (miR-290 cluster controls de novo DNA methylation via Rbl2/Dnmt3 in mouse ESCs)

effect: Dual/opposing roles reported in neural stem cell fate: represses TLX to promote differentiation while other reported activity supports proliferation — a feedback loop rather than a one-directional effect.
caveat: Not included in this file's explicit context-dependent flag list, but the underlying biology (a feedback loop with opposing arms) is functionally similar to the flagged entries — worth treating with the same caution even though it isn't formally tagged that way here.
keyCitation: Zhao, Sun, Li & Shi, 2009, Nat Struct Mol Biol (miR-9/TLX feedback loop in neural stem cell fate determination)

effect: Pro-angiogenic — suppresses HGS-mediated degradation of growth factor receptors (VEGFR2, PDGFRβ), increasing their surface availability.
caveat: Most of the primary literature for this miRNA is tumor-angiogenesis research, not regenerative medicine — included here because the mechanism (angiogenic receptor recycling) is directly relevant to regenerative vascularization, but the source literature's intent was oncology, and that context should travel with any citation of it.
keyCitation: Würdinger et al., 2008, Cancer Cell (miR-296 regulates growth-factor-receptor overexpression in angiogenic endothelial cells)
